subject: Auto-burst guardrail & short-window grace credit — proposal and next steps
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex@finable.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Subject: Quick question — can we get an automated burst buffer for next week's launch?

Soojin,

We have a probability spike next Tuesday when we flip a large customer to production. Our current quota will almost certainly be exceeded for a ~3 hour window. Two asks: 1) can Redwood temporarily raise rate limits for that window, and 2) is there an option for a short-term grace credit so we don’t get a punitive overrun invoice while we monitor? We can share a usage snapshot if it helps.

We’re fine with a one-off true-up, but would prefer an automated fallback that triggers without us having to chase billing during launch.

—Alex
VP, Engineering
Finable AI

---

On Tue, 11 Aug 2026 at 09:38 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai> wrote:
To: Alex Moreno <alex@finable.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Subject: Re: Quick question — can we get an automated burst buffer for next week's launch?

Alex — thanks for the heads up, and congrats on the rollout. Short answer: yes, we can.

Suggested approach (high level):
- Enable an opt-in "auto-burst guardrail" for the launch window (timebox start/end you pick).
- Provide a short-window grace credit: first 10% of overrun or the first 3 hours (whichever is smaller) will be covered by a one-time launch credit; anything beyond is billed at standard overrun rates.
- Add an automatic metering rule so we email ops + billing at 50%/100%/150% thresholds in real time.

I’ve attached a first-pass terms pdf and a quick usage CSV you sent earlier (redacted) for reference. If the credit approach looks good, we can prep a short amendment and a DocuSign link so legal doesn't block the go.

Questions for you:
1) Exact start/end for the window (local timezone)
2) Expected peak qps or token baseline (so Ben can size the buffer)
3) Whether you want the buffer to be auto-enabled or require a one-click confirmation from your admin on launch day.

I’ll loop in Ben for pricing math and Laura for approval/contract language.

—Soojin
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

---

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Moreno <alex@finable.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Subject: Re: Quick question — can we get an automated burst buffer for next week's launch?

Thanks — quick pricing note from my side:
- For a short-window temporary uplift we can offer a blended overrun rate that's 20% below standard list for any usage that falls into the guardrail buffer.
- The launch credit we cover: up to $3k USD of overrun (applied before billing) for one event per rolling 90-day period.
- If Finable wants a heavier buffer (e.g., sustained +24h headroom), we should move to a committed short-term uplift with a minimum monthly commit to protect capacity.

If Soojin confirms the exact window and targets, I’ll run the numbers and send a final price table (tokens / blended rate / credit applied).

—Ben
Commercial Lead, Redwood Inference

---

From: Alex Moreno <alex@finable.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 10:30:00 -07:00
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, procurement@finable.ai
Subject: Re: Quick question — can we get an automated burst buffer for next week's launch?

Thanks, Soojin and Ben. Window is 2026-08-18 02:00 - 2026-08-18 06:00 UTC (we're in PST, so that'll be late evening for us). Expected baseline is ~120 QPS, estimated peak could hit 600 QPS for short intervals (30–90 minutes). We want the buffer to be auto-enabled — engineers won't have time to click during the cutover.

Two clarifications:
- Can the credit be applied as a line-item adjustment on the next invoice (so our finance team sees a single reconciliation)?
- We may want a short post-mortem where you share the per-minute spike CSV so our SREs can tune.

Happy to sign a one-page amendment if you send it.

—Alex

---

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
To: Alex Moreno <alex@finable.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, procurement@finable.ai
Subject: Re: Quick question — can we get an automated burst buffer for next week's launch?

Alex — that works. Summary of proposed operational and billing plan (we'll put into a one-page amendment):
1) Auto-burst guardrail window: 2026-08-18T02:00Z to 2026-08-18T06:00Z (auto-enabled per your request).
2) Buffer sizing: we’ll provide capacity to tolerate up to 5x baseline for short bursts (benchmarked by Ben).
3) Grace credit: Redwood applies a one-time launch credit of up to $3,000 USD to the next invoice; credit applies to overrun charges first.
4) Blended overrun rate: any usage that exceeds the covered credit within the window will be billed at a blended overrun rate of list_rate * 0.8.
5) Alerts & telemetry: automated emails at 50% / 100% / 150% of baseline to Alex + Finable procurement + Redwood ops; post-event we’ll share a per-minute CSV and a short annotated spike timeline.
6) One event per rolling 90-day period; additional events require a separate amendment.

Laura — can you confirm legal is good with the line-item credit approach (billing team wants a single invoice reconciliation) and whether we need a separate MSA amendment or a short SOW will suffice?

If you all confirm, I’ll generate the DocuSign packet and Ben will attach the price table.

—Soojin

---

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 11:13:00 -07:00
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Moreno <alex@finable.ai>, procurement@finable.ai
Subject: Re: Quick question — can we get an automated burst buffer for next week's launch?

All — legal is okay with a one-page amendment that references the current MSA and describes the window, buffer terms, credit amount, and reporting commitments. Billing confirms they can apply the $3,000 credit as a line-item on the next invoice and will provide a reconciliation memo showing pre-credit charges, credit applied, and final amount.

Two asks from my side before DocuSign:
1) Add a short clause that we will not be liable for third-party downstream costs if Finable replays traffic or re-ingests the same payloads causing duplicate billing.
2) Confirm a single point of contact in Finable for invoice signoff (procurement@finable.ai is fine, but we prefer a named approver).

Once those are in, please send to DocuSign.

—Laura
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference
